feedback: Iteration 0 gives the main evidence. All 60 trials (oval, s-bend and slalom) ended off track, with progress of 0.105 to 0.156 and mean max_error of 0.061 to 0.062 m, just above the 0.06 m limit. Line-loss events were only 1 to 2 per run, so the 40 mm sensor spread still sees the tape, and the drift is late reaction rather than sensing failure. Your move to y=0.06 m is therefore the right first step. I have raised steering gain in the controller to compensate for weak correction (kp 2.0, kd 0.3), so the geometry itself does not need changing before this race. I state no outcome for the y=0.06 m geometry. For the next iteration: if the race shows max_error still at or above 0.06 m with progress below 0.2, the limit is probably controller gain or speed, not geometry, so hold the geometry and do not widen it. If line_loss_events rise on the sharpest bend (above about 2 per run), the spread is then too narrow, and widening to +/-0.032 m becomes the next option. Holding the spread at +/-0.024 m is correct while line losses stay low.
requested_changes: Hold the sensors at y=0.06 m with x of +/-0.024 m and the same sensor size for the next race, to test the forward offset alone.
If max_error stays at or above 0.06 m with progress below 0.2 after this race, hold the geometry and let the Integrator tune gain. Do not change the body or mass yet.
If line_loss_events rise above about 2 per run on the sharpest bend, widen the sensor spread to x = +/-0.032 m with five sensors, and keep y=0.06 m.
